Emergency · act now

Emergency quick actions

First aid team / Call for help Call the first aid team for an ambulance / urgent chemical incident (fire, uncontrolled spill/gas release, injury). Call for help for advice when it is not immediately life-threatening.

Assess → Respond → Manage

Assess: hazards, injuries. Respond if safe to make safe (minimal risk, you have the expertise/resources) — isolate, secure, contain, ventilate, shut off ignition/fuel sources, treat casualties, monitor.

If NOT safe (evident risk, you lack the expertise/resources): evacuate, send for specialist assistance, treat casualties as quickly as possible, secure the area & inform others.

Never put yourself or others at risk. After: RECORD, REPORT, REVIEW and UPDATE procedures.

Fire & spills

  • Fire — not safe: Evacuate & isolate the area. Call for help.
  • Fire — safe: Cut off ignition/fuel sources and extinguish, only if trained and confident.
  • Spill — not safe: Isolate/secure the area. Call the first aid team for advice, or call for help in extreme cases.
  • Spill — safe: Check the Hazcard, wear correct PPE, then Assess → Contain → Collect → Treat → Dispose. Clean up, check own clothes/skin, wash thoroughly.

Calling for help: have ready — chemical identity, how it's contained, quantity, and any hazard info, without delaying the call.

Chemical exposure — IRM

RouteImmediate action
EyeIRRIGATE 20+ min. Severe symptoms → call for help. Otherwise → call the first aid team. Keep irrigating until told to stop.
MouthRINSE & SPIT, don't swallow or induce vomiting. Severe symptoms → call for help, else call the first aid team.
InhaledMOVE TO FRESH AIR, sit/support. Severe symptoms → call for help, else call the first aid team. Watch for delayed effects.
SkinIRRIGATE 20+ min, remove contaminated clothing/jewellery while irrigating. No "neutralising" chemicals. Severe symptoms → call for help, else call the first aid team.

Always check the specific Hazcard — some chemicals need extra measures.

Non-chemical emergencies

  • Hair/clothing on fire: Stop, drop & roll, or smother with a fire blanket.
  • Burns/scalds: Cool under gently running water 20+ minutes.
  • Severe cuts: Apply pressure, raise the wound, don't remove embedded objects.
  • Asthma / anaphylaxis: Support & protect; help access their medication.
  • Fainting / fit / unconscious: Lower gently, protect from injury, recovery position if unconscious.
  • Electric shock: Isolate from supply (switch off, or use an insulator). Call for help.

Quick Reference

Storage & waste codes, pictograms, IRM glossary

From safety reference GL120

These are searched together with the box above — e.g. try searching "CLa", "W4" or "irrigate".

Storage codes

16
Situ Make only when needed — do not store

Dispose of immediately after preparation and use. Do not store; these chemicals may rapidly degrade or become unstable.

Spec Special case — check Hazcard

Particular storage needs; require periodic inspection as they are prone to deterioration, may release toxic/corrosive vapours and/or build up pressure. Replace container/cap immediately if damaged or leaking.

Rad Radioactive

See Managing ionising radiations and radioactive substances (Guide L93).

Cyl Gas cylinder (or canister)

Compressed, liquefied or dissolved gases. Never store flammables in the same room as gas cylinders or radioactives. Keep away from oxidising agents.

FL Flammable liquid

Flash point ≤ 60°C. Up to 50 L may be kept in a fire-resistant cupboard in an adequately ventilated prep room or store.

FW Flammable, water-reactive

E.g. alkali metals. Keep in a separate box/cupboard away from water and water-based reagents. Do NOT store with flammable liquids or in the flammables cupboard.

FS Flammable solid

E.g. red phosphorus. Keep on shelves with General Inorganics (GIn) or in a secure cupboard. Not next to oxidising agents (Ox). Not with flammable liquids.

CLa Corrosive liquid (acid)

Good ventilation essential. Keep low down/at floor level, protected from being knocked over. Keep as far as possible from the CLb group (non-acids).

CLb Corrosive liquid (non-acid)

Store away from CLa (acids), even if just at opposite ends of the same store.

CW Corrosive, water-reactive

Produces fumes in contact with moist air. Usually kept inside another container with a suitable fume-absorbing agent. Check the Hazcard.

CS Corrosive solid

Usually kept with general chemicals (GIn/GOrg).

Cold Cold storage (refrigerator)

Materials that degrade or have short shelf lives at room temperature, e.g. enzymes.

T Toxic

May be kept with general chemicals (GIn/GOrg) provided the store is secure against unauthorised access; otherwise use a separate locked cupboard.

Ox Oxidising agent

Usually stored with general inorganic chemicals (GIn). Keep away from all flammable (FL, FW, FS) or combustible (GOrg) chemicals.

GIn General chemical (inorganic)

General storage group for inorganic chemicals with no higher-priority hazard.

GOrg General chemical (organic)

General storage group for organic chemicals with no higher-priority hazard. Keep separate from Ox to avoid combustible materials near oxidisers.

Waste disposal codes

9
W1 Store for removal by a Registered Waste Carrier

For significant quantities of any hazardous chemical. Must NOT go down the drain or into normal refuse. Includes unwanted stock and some absorbed/collected spills.

W2 Collect and store for removal by a Registered Waste Carrier

Small quantities that cannot be treated/recycled in-house. Keep SEPARATE labelled containers for: mercury metal/compounds (incl. broken thermometers); lead/cadmium metal & compounds; silver residues (never mix with organic waste); organohalogens (never mix with other organic waste); water-insoluble flammable liquids/other organics (excl. organohalogens).

W3 Recycle or re-use the material

Small amounts of waste that can easily and safely be re-used or recycled. Check the Hazcard.

W4 Neutralise and dilute — substance reacts with alkalis

Add slowly to 1 M sodium carbonate solution (heat/spray may be produced). Test with indicator, adding more sodium carbonate until just alkaline. Pour down a foul-water drain with further dilution.

W5 Neutralise and dilute — substance reacts with acids

Add slowly to 1 M ethanoic acid solution (heat/spray may be produced). Test with indicator, adding more ethanoic acid until just acidic. Pour down a foul-water drain with further dilution.

W6 Evaporate, burn or vent in a working fume cupboard

For small amounts of some volatile chemicals. Use a ducted fume cupboard where possible (or out in the open if safe). Placing residues in a shallow tray speeds evaporation.

W7 Pour down a foul-water drain

For small amounts of water-soluble chemicals — dilute to below the concentration given on the Hazcard first. If dilution would need much more than 8 L (a bucketful), consider pre-treatment (W4/W5) first.

W8 Place in the normal refuse

NEVER for EXPLOSIVE, FLAMMABLE or OXIDISING chemicals. Only if the hazardous component's concentration is below the W8 table limit. Deliberate dilution with an inert solid (e.g. sand) is NOT permitted.

WSpec Special disposal requirements

Follow the specific instructions given on the individual Hazcard for this chemical.

Hazard pictograms (GHS)

9
GHS01 Explosive

Can cause explosions under conditions such as shock, friction, fire/ignition or heat. Contact the school\u2019s safety officer if a purchased chemical carries this pictogram.

GHS02 Flammable

Gases, aerosols, liquids and solids, incl. self-reactive/self-heating, pyrophoric (ignite on air exposure), and chemicals that emit flammable gas in contact with water.

GHS03 Oxidising

Can cause or contribute to combustion or explosion of other materials. May not be combustible itself.

GHS04 Gas under pressure

Compressed, liquefied or dissolved gases in cylinders/canisters, and refrigerated liquefied gases.

GHS05 Corrosive

+DANGER = capable of severe skin burns and eye damage, or serious eye damage. +WARNING = may be corrosive to metals.

GHS06 Acute toxicity

Potential to cause serious harm (possibly fatal) after even a small, single or short exposure by ingestion, inhalation or skin/eye contact.

GHS07 Moderate health hazard

Irritant (skin/eye/respiratory), skin sensitiser, harmful by ingestion/inhalation/contact, or narcotic effects (drowsiness/dizziness). +WARNING also used for ozone-depleting chemicals.

GHS08 Serious health hazard

Respiratory sensitisers, specific organ toxicity, aspiration hazard; carcinogenic, mutagenic, and/or toxic to reproduction (CMR).

GHS09 Hazardous to the aquatic environment

May cause short- or long-term effects in water. Avoid release to the environment whenever possible.

Emergency response (IRM) terms

14
Immediate

Key to minimising harm — respond as soon as you become aware of exposure.

Irrigate

Flood the affected area with gently-running water, even if the chemical reacts with water — plenty of water minimises damage.

Irrigate (skin)

Use only water unless the chemical adheres to skin (then liquid soap if immediately available). Remove as much chemical as possible first only if it won't delay irrigation.

Irrigate (eyes)

Direct water via clean tubing from a tap, or plumbed-in eyewash, for an effective flow. Continue until told to stop by the first aid team.

More than 20 minutes

Continue irrigation until the first aid team advises you can stop.

Rinse and spit

Give clean drinking water, rinse around the mouth (do NOT swallow) and spit out. Do not induce vomiting.

Move to fresh air

Help the casualty away from the chemical source into fresh air (not outdoors if cold/wet).

Delayed effects

Absence of immediate symptoms does not mean no damage occurred — symptoms may appear later, even after days.

Call for help

Do not hesitate, regardless of symptoms — the chemical may cause severe harm quickly or without obvious signs.

Corrosive (IRM note)

Can cause severe, permanent tissue damage. Inhalation/ingestion may swell mouth, throat or airways. Call the first aid team and continue IRM until advised otherwise.

Alkali (IRM note)

May cause serious damage with no obvious symptoms. Treat as urgent regardless of symptoms. Call for help.

Oxidising (IRM note)

Can cause burns and systemic effects if absorbed. Ensure ALL traces are removed from skin, eyes and clothing.

Toxic (IRM note)

Even a relatively small dose can cause serious harm.

CMR

Carcinogen / Mutagen / Reproductive hazard. A single exposure is unlikely to be significant, but consult a doctor if concerned.
